content: The Founder points at item 3 on the board. 'Archive 002 should come first. If we name it, half of these go quiet. People stop asking about the tee when they're excited about the next thing.' He says it flatly, like someone who has already decided.

Head of Product doesn't move item 3. They draw arrows to reorder the board instead. 'Respectfully, no. If we announce Archive 002 on top of a dead seed with no remedy, it's the same blind prepay with a nicer first chapter. That's the skeptic's line from the report. Agenda: dead marigold, refund policy, delivery date, trust gap, scarcity and proof, tin versus plant, specs, the collector-gift split, and Archive 002 last, when we know what we're promising. Each one gets an owning role. Then we score everything on impact, cost, effort and confidence.'

decisions.text: Agenda order: PP1 dead marigold, PP2 refund policy, PP9 delivery date, PP4 trust gap, PP6 scarcity/proof, PP7 tin vs plant, PP5 specs, PP8 collector vs gift split, PP3 Archive 002 product and price; then scoring on impact, cost, effort, confidence

content: Research raises a hand, but it isn't a question. 'Item 8 hangs on your survey, and we don't know its details: who was asked, how many people, what the questions were. Before we reach item 8, can I see the questions? I'm not trying to catch you out. Right now it's the only real-person data we have, and I can't weigh it without seeing it.'

proposals.text: Founder shares the survey questions and recruitment method with Research before PP8 is discussed

content: Brand caps the marker HoP left on the table and taps item 7. 'Put me down for tin versus plant, and I want it before specs. If we don't know what the product is, we'll write the wrong spec card.'

The Designer writes their role into the owner boxes for items 1 and 5 without asking. 'Physical side of the dead seed, the insert and the unboxing, and the spec card. I'll bring proposals, not specs. Tin size and tee fabric are still UNKNOWN.'
The Plant Specialist nods across the table to CX. 'You and me on item 1. You handle what happens after a seed fails. I'll try to make fewer of them fail. Joint owners.'

Growth looks at Archive 002 at the bottom of the list and works it out: if the Founder accepts this order, the announcement is still at least a few weeks away. They decide to use every agenda item to argue for something that can go into the funnel this week.

Community claims items 4 and 6 and draws a line linking them. 'Trust gap and proof of legitimacy are one story told twice. The collector lead in the report only bought after the reseller rumour got a straight answer. I'd like to run them back to back.'
CX writes their name under item 2 and turns to Finance, half smiling. 'Fair warning. I'm going to ask for a written refund-or-replacement promise. You'll have your worst case ready?'

Ops finally steps away from the packing bench. 'Item 9 is mine. And so we're clear about the 8-week plan for Archive 002: I haven't timed how long hand-painting 100 tins takes. Nobody has. Until I do, every date in this room is a guess.'

Finance doesn't look up from the notebook. 'I'll have a worst case once Ops tells me what a seed packet and a reshipment cost. What I know right now is Rs 1,099 a unit and Rs 1,09,900 gross on a full run. That's the whole envelope.'
From the laptop: 'Put me as reviewer on 2, 4 and 9, and on any growth claim about scarcity or urgency. I'll mark everything verify with a professional.'
